body:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected: elevated 5xxs on /v1/chat.generate in us-west-2 (routing fallback activated) — paging oncall group. initial alert at 1768429167
Samir: getting the page. I see a spike of 502/503s and a note in routing logs: requests are being routed from model `redwood-chat-v2` to `redwood-instruct-quant` as fallback. that variant is `instruct`-style, incompatible with chat payload (function calls + messages) — likely causes schema errors.
Marta: ack. i'm on it. tagging @oncall-rotation to hand off. any active deploys?
oncall-rotation: no deploys listed in last 30m.
Samir: paste of recent routing entry:
```
{"ts":"1768429120","req_id":"r-8a7f","route":"chat.generate","pinned_variant":"redwood-chat-v2","fallback":"redwood-instruct-quant","reason":"capacity_exhausted"}
```
Marta: that `fallback` is wrong for chat endpoints — it should be a compat chat variant (e.g., `redwood-chat-quant`) not an instruct model. i suspect a policy gap in smart-routing -> variant compatibility checks.
Eli: joining. i'm pulling the control-plane policy for customer-facing routing.
Eli: running `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://control-plane/api/routing/policies/us-west-2`
Eli: snippet (sanitized):
```
- route: /v1/chat.generate
  priority: latency
  pins: [redwood-chat-v2]
  fallbacks: [redwood-instruct-quant, redwood-embed-lite]
```
Jess: oh. fallbacks has instruct and embed variants mixed in. that is wrong. looks like a policy edit earlier this week added a generic fallback list without model-family checks.
Samir: impact estimate: chat.generate 5xx rate up to 18% for rps peaks in us-west-2. customer-success flagged 2 paying customers: acme-corp and hopscotch-app — both on chat endpoints; embeddings endpoints unaffected.
customer-success: acme-corp reported: "chat responses failing with \"unexpected payload: messages must be a list\"". they have a canary of 25% of traffic in us-west-2.
Marta: mitigation path A (fast): remove instruct/embedding fallbacks from chat routes so requests don't go to incompatible variants (fail open to model-unavailable -> trigger retry) — better than routing to incompatible variant. mitigation path B: create temp pin to redwood-chat-quant (compatible) and increase capacity.
Samir: i can remove fallbacks now. that will cause requests to either remain pinned or hit the region-wide fallback tier. any objections?
Eli: go for it, but alert customers that some requests may get transient errors until we pin a compatible variant. coordinate with customer-success.
Marta: executing control-plane change: `PATCH /api/routing/policies/us-west-2` payload:
```
- op: replace
  path: /routes/chat.generate/fallbacks
  value: []
```
Marta: done. change applied at 1768430020.
deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: routing-policy-us-west-2 updated by marta at 1768430020 (change-id: ch-9832).
Samir: monitoring: 5xx dropped from 18% -> 3% in 3 minutes. latency stable. no new errors about unexpected payload.
customer-success: notified acme-corp and hopscotch-app with status update. acme said "seeing improvement, thanks".
Eli: next step: pin a compatible fallback with margin: `redwood-chat-quant` on the policy and ensure model-family validation prevents non-chat variants in chat routes. i'll open a PR to add validation + an automated test.
Jess: also need a migration to sweep existing policies for mixed-family fallbacks. i'll file infra task.
Samir: creating incident ticket: INC-2026-3099 and adding postmortem owner.
Samir: quick root-cause sketch: a config push earlier this week added a generic fallback set used by multiple routes. it didn't enforce model_family compatibility. when chat-chat capacity hit a transient low, smart-routing applied the generic fallback list and selected `redwood-instruct-quant`, which returned schema errors.
Marta: post-incident notes:
- mitigation: removed incompatible fallbacks (temporary) at 1768430020
- mitigation: customers notified (acme-corp, hopscotch-app) at 1768430125
- followups: add policy-family validation, patch control-plane to reject fallbacks with mismatched model_family, audit existing policies, add e2e test for chat -> instruct mismatch.
Eli: estimate effort: validation + tests ~2-3 engineer-days; policy sweep ~1 day; release to prod next week.
Jess: assigning followups: SRE (marta) to run policy sweep, ML infra (eli) to add validation, product (samir) to coordinate customer comms + SLA impact.
Samir: marking incident as mitigated at 1768431200. we'll keep monitoring for 2h.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: INCIDENT mitigated (mitigation timestamp: 1768431200). severity: P2. link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-3099
Marta: creating postmortem doc and will drop link here when ready. thanks all for fast turnaround. :heart:
